'''Richard Eugene Barlow''' (January 12, 1931 – 2024) was an American mathematician and mathematical statistician, who is considered with [[Frank Proschan]] as the founder of modern [[reliability engineering|reliability theory]]. He was a professor at the [[University of California, Berkeley]] from 1963 until his retirement in 1999.

He introduced the concept of "Total Time on Test" processes in reliability theory.<ref name="YuZalkind2001">{{cite book|author1=Hayakawa Yu|author2=Irony Telba Zalkind|author3=Xie Min|title=System And Bayesian Reliability: Essays In Honor Of Professor Richard E Barlow On His 70th Birthday|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=t9TUCgAAQBAJ&pg=PA123|date=21 December 2001|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=978-981-4489-34-8}}</ref> He and Proschan cowrote the book ''Mathematical Theory of Reliability''.

==Biography==
Barlow received his bachelor's degree in mathematics from [[Knox College (Illinois)|Knox College]] in 1953 and his master's degree in mathematics from the [[University of Oregon]] in 1955.<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard E. Barlow |url=https://www.informs.org/Explore/History-of-O.R.-Excellence/Biographical-Profiles/Barlow-Richard-E |website=Informs |access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> In 1961 he received his doctorate in mathematical statistics from [[Stanford University]] under [[Samuel Karlin]]. His dissertation was titled ''Applications of Semi-Markov Processes to Counter and Reliability Problems''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard Barlow |url=https://genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=46566 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |access-date=18 August 2019}}</ref> After graduation, he worked at the [[Institute for Defense Analyses]] for a year. He was from 1963 until his retirement in 1999 a professor at UC Berkeley. While at Berkeley, he mentored several doctoral students in [[operations research]].

He was a guest scientist at the Boeing Laboratories in 1966 and at Florida State University in 1975 and 1976 (with Frank Proschan). From 1963 to 1969 he was an advisor to the [[Rand Corporation]].

In addition to reliability theory, he dealt with probabilistic modeling in Bayesian statistics and statistical data analysis.

In 1991 he was awarded the [[John von Neumann Theory Prize]] with Frank Proschan. He is a Fellow of the [[Institute of Mathematical Statistics]], the [[American Statistical Association]], and the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]].

==Personal life and death==
He is married since 1956 and has four children.

Barlow died in 2024, at the age of 92–93.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Negelev |first=Goldie |date=2025-05-27 |title=In Memoriam: Richard E. Barlow (1931–2024) |url=https://ieor.berkeley.edu/in-memoriam-richard-e-barlow-1931-2024/ |access-date=2026-01-09 |website=UC Berkeley IEOR Department - Industrial Engineering & Operations Research |language=en-US}}</ref>
